utterances.text: There's not. Mr. Guy-Smith raised this with us previously and that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. "With regard to the witness yesterday, the Prosecutor agrees and admits that the witness L-04 was shown a photo spread of six photographs by investigators from CCIU/UNMIK at some point in time between January and March 2002. In the photo spread of six separate photographs, there was a single photograph of Haradin Bala, an accused in this case. Witness L-04 was unable to recognise any person in the series of six photographs." That is the first of the agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could I just make it clear, Mr. Bakrac, that that has nothing to do with you or your evidence. That's an entirely different issue, in case you're confused about what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I now am going to read into the record an agreed fact that does have something to do with Mr. Bakrac, and that is as follows: "On January 8th and 9th of 2002, in that time, Mr. Bakrac was shown a series of photographs. And with regard to photo spread A1, his comments were as follows: 'Number 2 looks familiar, but I don't know from where and I cannot connect him with this case. With regard to photo spread A2, no one looks familiar. With regard to photo spread A3, no one looks familiar.'" I had previously presented the Court with a proposed number of exhibits that included A4 and A5, however for purposes of the specific examination that I was going to engage in with Mr. Bakrac after having received this agreement from the Office of the Prosecutor, I don't believe that we need to go any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: However, I trust that each of you has a copy of that particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have the first of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not aware of having a note of the second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have the photographs? Excellent. The agreement reached was reached but moments before Your Honours came into court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now we understand. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bakrac. My name is Gregor Guy-Smith and I represent Haradin Bala. I would like to take but a bit of your time and ask you but a few questions. Is that all right, sir?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is all right. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the event that I ask you a question which is incomprehensible and which you don't understand for any reason, please let me know and I will rephrase it. As I understand your testimony, sir, you were at this place for a number of days. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you indicated that at some point in time you saw an individual who you learned was named "Shala" who was wearing, I believe, a black hat. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have in mind the photograph that my colleague Mr. Topolski just showed you but moments ago, in which individuals were wearing black caps?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that the hat or type of that the that you were referring to when you saw this individual named Shala wearing a black hat?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't state that with any certainty. I don't remember if it was the same, but it seems to me that it did have insignia on it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say it had insignia on it, could you by any chance help us by describing that insignia in any fashion whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the insignia of the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, could you tell us what that insignia was, if you remember. Was it letters? Numbers?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was red and black. Now, as to what the letters were on it, I don't know and I didn't look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You also have told us that when you were in I believe it was the basement, you had an opportunity to have a conversation with at least some of the men who were in the basement room. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you learned that some of them were Serbians. True?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question fully. Yes, they were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you learned that some of the people, there were three in the room, who were Albanians. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They spent most of the time sleeping?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You did not speak with them?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None of the men in that room had been beaten, had they?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for Genov and Cuk, before. As for that room, only Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is information that none of the men in that room, except for the ones that you've just mentioned, sir, this is information you received from people that you talked to in that room. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely. You learned that the men who were in the room - and I'm excluding, as you rightly pointed out, two gentlemen - had not been beaten. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You learned from the men in the room how long they'd been there, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And both the Serbian men and the Albanian men had been there for a considerable period of time; that's what you were told?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Serbs had been there seven days and the Albanians a bit longer than that. I did know that fact, but I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you came here to testify, you spoke with your son about your experiences, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we never spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The reason that I'm asking you that question is in your testimony today you use some very specific language with regard to a question that had been asked of you by Mr. Black, and the question which is on page 23, I believe line 19, occurring at 15:17:42, was: "And did that eventually happen?" And your answer some six seconds later was: "Yes, it did. It was in the early evening -- it was in the early evening. We were sitting in the room. Two gunshots were heard. Ivan and I remember that." When I heard you say "Ivan and I remember that," that made me think that when you were testifying here about this incident that you were also in your own mind thinking about a conversation that you had with your son. So when I asked you the question earlier, and I'll ask you the question again. Before you came here today did you have an opportunity or did you speak with your son Ivan about your experiences?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not speak about it. What I said, that Ivan and had heard it, I said that we had both heard it because we were both present there. Now, as to whether he actually remembers that at this point I don't know. Because from the moment of our release until this day, nobody could speak to Ivan about these events. I couldn't speak either. Yesterday when I got out of the courtroom, today, we did not speak a word. The only thing he asked me was, Are you through? And I said, No, not yet. That's the full extent of my conversation with my son about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You are aware, of course, that your son has spoken with investigators about this matter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you're also aware that your son has, as a matter of fact, alerted investigators to information that he has found with regard to this matter, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What are you talking about? What -- Ivan has found what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That Ivan has been involved in looking at websites concerning this matter?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fair enough. This man Shala, this is a man who, as I understand your testimony, you saw quite frequently. True?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is a man you spoke to on more than one occasion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is a man who brought you food. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is a man who brought you cigarettes because you did smoke. Right?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is a man who you looked directly at in your conversation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you spoke with him, you were certainly closer to him than you and I are to each other right now. Right?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, thank you very much for your time and for your candour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Earlier, Mr. Bakrac, I believe you told one of the Defence attorneys that you didn't look at those people because you were afraid, and I think you were referring to soldiers at the farm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I just want to be clear. When you spoke with Shala, did you look directly at him?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always look at people I talk to. This means that I looked at him, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about the person who came to talk Ivan from the basement, the one you think was a superior? Did you look directly at him when you spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to him in the same way, as I usually do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I'm able to say that's the end of your questioning and your evidence. The Chamber would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance you've given us and you're free now to go back to your place of living. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if I might just mention one matter very briefly before the next witness joins us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I had raised this with Mr. Black at the end of our session last night, and I was hoping that he might deal with it today. Perhaps it's simply an oversight on his part or perhaps intentional, I don't know. Your Honours, I don't know if you have a transcript of yesterday before you. It's page 71 of the uncorrected version that I have in front of me. And I raise this hoping that it can be resolved without the necessity of recalling the witness who's just left us, although I'm conscious that he won't be leaving The Hague, no doubt, until his son does. Your Honours, at page 71 line 2, this is Mr. Black in chief, and he says this: "At the beginning of your testimony I asked you about statements that you'd given previously to the ICTY and to another organisation, the Humanitarian Law Centre. Do you remember that -- do you remember those questions of mine? "A. Yes. "Q. Do you remember if in those statements you also described this person that you've now told us was beating Genov? "A. I think so. "Q. Do you think you described him essentially the way you've just described him now? "A. Yes." I, of course, have the advantage over the Court in that the -- I don't think the Court has the Humanitarian Law Centre's statement, anything other than produced to it, and therefore Your Honours haven't read it. The point is that the nature of the description in that statement to the Humanitarian Law Centre is significantly different and briefer than the statement -- the description the witness gives which Mr. Black elicited from his ICTY statement. What I was hoping might be corrected was the impression that could be thought to have been left by Mr. Black's questions and the answers he got from the witness yesterday. It's not been done. I'm content to leave the matter where it stands. The witness has given his evidence and given his description, but when one goes over the transcripts as one does, perhaps not just now but in the future, there is there left hanging an assertion which we would respectfully submit is not made out by a consideration of the material. I simply want to make that observation so the Court is aware of it. I'm entirely in the Court's hands how it would wish to handle it, if at all, hereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You didn't think to pursue it in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, no, I didn't because I was as it were content with the answers the witnesses had given. Perhaps I should have done. Perhaps I should have put to him the briefer one-liner, actually from the previous statement. Now, if the Court thinks that's the right and better and fairer way of doing it, then with my humble apologies for not doing it, Mr. Bakrac could be brought back and I could do just that. Otherwise an impression is left hanging. Now I'd hoped Mr. Black was simply going to say something today, but he clearly felt -- thought better of it or forgot. I don't know. But that's where matters are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: In fairness to my learned friend, Mr. Black, of course you will remember that the reason why that document is not before you is not because of any lack of effort on the part of my learned friend sitting opposite, it was because it was objected to by at least two members on this side of the table. Your Honour, I take -- these cases of course are big enough and difficult enough, and I think it is important to keep some structure to them. I would accordingly oppose any trend that could be set in motion of recalling witnesses when a party has had a chance to ask some relevant questions. This witness gave evidence yesterday. We were given the transcripts and the LiveNote overnight. We had a chance to go through those transcripts overnight. And of course the whole purpose of cross-examination is to test the evidence that has been given. Now, Your Honour, the reason I'm objecting is for the same reason that I objected for that document to go in. It's a matter of principle, because if one starts being somewhat slack in the rules, if I can put it like that, we can get into all kinds of difficulties down the road. And I think I would object if Mr. Black had sought to recall one of his witnesses to fill in an omission or an apparent omission. And I think as a matter of principle I have to stand firm on this issue, even though it's for my learned friend, and say that I have to take exactly the same position with my learned colleague on this side of the bench -- or the bar as I would for the Prosecution. And for those bases as a matter of principle, I have to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, my apologies to Mr. Topolski. I'm afraid I didn't grasp exactly what he was trying to say to me last night. So it wasn't intentional that I didn't raise this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. matter, although I think it could be left as it is. If Mr. Bakrac is going to be called back in, I simply ask that happen now and there be no chance that he be asked to come back at a later time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I withdraw the application to recall Mr. Bakrac, even if I made it. I think I'll be able to deal with this as an agreed fact in due course. I see the sensitivities. I have to say in passing I don't think if I put one line of that statement to the humanitarian organisation to the witness I would put the whole document in, or even begin to do so. But I appreciate the sensitivity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You never know, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You never know. Age and experience has taught me never to be sure about these things. Your Honour, therefore I don't pursue that aspect of it. Forgive me for taking up the Court's time. It remains a slight concern, but I'm sure with goodwill on both sides Mr. Black and I can agree the position without the necessity of recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Topolski. Can I just venture, Mr. Khan, that the Chamber will look at the merits of each application --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There are certain circumstances when recall because of oversight is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I was simply looking at matters of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The occasion, for the moment, has passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I say one thing which I think is purely administrative. With regard to this exhibit that was labelled 77 for identification only hasn't been tendered again into evidence. I just want to make sure wherever that is on the system if it could be under seal, because there are references in there that are not public. So I don't know when an exhibit is marked for identification if it goes on to the Internet or what happens to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not an exhibit. It's a document that has been identified, is in the custody of the Chamber. And if it becomes of relevance, if the document previously identified is able to be produced and authenticated by its custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I understand that and I'm not challenging or meaning to have to touch on that at all. I would simply just like to say if the registrar has this, perhaps he doesn't, if it's anywhere available on the record that it not be public, because there are references on it that should not be public. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the registrar read the words "under seal."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: To the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can now rest this evening and you'll sleep peacefully. Are we ready for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I believe we are, Your Honour. Mr. Nicholls can take the next witness. Could I be briefly excused? I need to attend to a matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've lost track. When will the next break be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. The answer was quarter of an hour or 20 minutes, on-air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bakrac, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to take the card that's in front of you and read the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bakrac. If you would sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls will now ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Can you hear me all right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Please remember, as I told you earlier, we're speaking in different languages. Everything we say is being translated into several languages, so it's important if you can to speak a little bit perhaps more slowly than we ordinarily would and to try to speak clearly. Okay?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you tell me your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Ivan Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were born in 1979. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Tell me your place of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Zagreb, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What ethnicity are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, before we go a little further, I want to talk just a little bit of background. You've given one written statement to investigators for the ICTY. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That was in January of 2003.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you came here recently to The Hague, to this city, and met with me, you met first with Investigator Lehtinen and Andrew Cayley. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then you met with me Tuesday for a brief time, and then also on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you watched this trial on television at all at any time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you watched it on the Internet at all? And I mean, watched the proceedings at all on the Internet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you followed this trial in the press, in newspapers or magazines?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Hardly ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: [In English] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Would you please tell me a little bit about your family. Who do you live with?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: With my parents and with my older brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you currently employed? You do not need to tell me what your job is, but -- where you're working, rather, but are you working at this time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you briefly outline for the Chamber and for counsel present your educational background. Again, you do not need to tell me the names of any schools you went to but just how far you went in school, what topics you studied, and if you got -- if you received any degrees or diplomas.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: After high school, I completed a four-year university degree in business.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you ever been in the military?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back and ask you some questions about when you were living in Zagreb, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In 19 -- well, could you tell me when your family left Croatia, what year.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that last answer. It wasn't heard properly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And very briefly, can you tell us why your family left Croatia that year.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Because of our ethnicity. Many Serb families left Croatia because of their Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did your whole family leave at once or -- did you all go together or did you go separately?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Separately. First my older brother and I, and then our parents came.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where did you go from Zagreb, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: To Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did your family spend in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, we're recording everything and maintaining a transcript. Sometimes it doesn't always get picked up. So I'd ask you wait a moment after I finish and then please repeat your answer, if you could. The question was, if I remember: How long did your family spend in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: A year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you describe very briefly what it was like that year, what kind of work your father did. If you can just tell us what it was like that year, what the family spent its time doing.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: We lived with my grandparents, my mother's parents. My father worked as a waiter and my mother worked as a hairdresser.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: After that period, where did your family move to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: To Djakovica, Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And why was that? Why did the family move there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: My father got a job at the hotel. Since it was not easy to live in Belgrade, we moved to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you were a teenager at this time. Could you describe, just briefly, what your life was like in Djakovica after you moved there, whether you went to school, what types of things you were interested in.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: When we moved to Djakovica I was very young. It was a time when you go to elementary school and then to high school. And like many other teenagers, I was interested in basketball, fishing, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you interested in politics?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me move ahead a little bit now to the year 1998. Could you describe what the atmosphere -- that's not a very good way of putting it. Could you describe at that point what it was like for your family living in Kosovo, in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, it was very hard because discussions have already started between the Serbs living in Kosovo and the Albanians. We noticed it was very hard to live that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you tell me about your friends, your personal friends, when you were living and going to school in Djakovica. What ethnicity were your friends, your close friends?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: There were Croats, Muslims, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you friends with Serbs as well as Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, when your family had moved to Djakovica and your father took that job at the hotel, was the plan that this was going to be a permanent relocation, that you would stay there, or were there any other plans that the family thought about for its future?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: At first our plan was to stay down there in Djakovica. Later on, only my father and my mother know ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you finished your answer, sir. Only your father and your mother knew what?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, they were the only ones who knew whether we would stay in Djakovica or go back to Croatia or Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, at the end of June 1998, if you remember, did your families -- did your family have any plans that month what it was going Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to do? Was there any event that a -- any steps that the family planned to take?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. There was plan for us to move out of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, without telling us, because it's not relevant, exactly where you were moving to, was the plan to stay within Kosovo or not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did your family begin to move anywhere at the end of June 1998?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you just describe how that move was to take place, the initial stages of that move.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What do you mean by initial stages or initial steps?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That was my fault. That wasn't a good question. I don't want you to talk about where any final destination that you planned to go to might be, but I want you to tell me if your family started on a journey anywhere from Djakovica to anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe that, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, since there were already major problems between the Albanians and all the rest who were non-Albanian, we decided to return to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how were you going to get there? How were you going to travel?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know it's a couple minutes early, but I wonder if we could break now. I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 5 minutes to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll continue now, Ivan, and let me just say again, if you feel a little nervous, that's fine. Just take your time to answer the questions. I don't want you to feel rushed at all. Okay? Now, just before the break you told us that the plan was to go to Serbia and was to go by bus from Djakovica at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, who from your family was on the bus when it -- when you got on it to start this journey?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: My father, my mother, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And as close as you remember, can you tell me where you and your family were sitting on the bus when it left -- or when you boarded it in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: My father and my mother sat right in the front, behind the driver. And I sat in the second row behind the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if you remember, what route was the bus going to take? Which towns was it going to go through on the way, if you know?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but it was supposed to go via Brezice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, during this time that we're talking about, the end of June 1998, was there any problem with transportation by road in this area? Were there any difficulties in getting from one place to another on the roads and highways?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Was -- were there -- well, let's just talk about the journey. The journey started. Did it make any unscheduled -- were there any unscheduled stops along the way?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. The bus stopped en route at a garage to fix the brakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you remember what town that was in?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it was near Prizren, before we got into the town of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you: How full was the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was quite full. I don't know if it was completely full, but it was quite full.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did the passengers do during this stop for repairs near Prizren? And I mean, did they stay on the bus or get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Many got off the bus in order to walk around a little bit or to smoke a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long was this delay?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Between 45 minutes and an hour, about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And once the bus started, what happened next on the journey? Was there anything else that was not planned or that sticks out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. We were stopped -- in fact, the driver stopped next to a Serbian police officer and asked whether it was safe to go through Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And why would he ask that question?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did the policeman tell him, tell the driver, if you could overhear that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: The police officer said that it was safer to go through Brezovica. The road was longer, but it was safer than the one via Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he say why it was safer or why he recommended taking that route, other than that it was just safer?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He just said that, but we all know, especially we Serbs know, why he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you explain that, your answer, please. Why did he say that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, he said that there were quite a few Albanian soldiers there and that it was not safe for the Serb -- Serbs to go there and take that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when the bus continued, which route did the driver take? Did he take the route recommended by the Serbian police officer or a different route?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. He took a different route through Prizren and some other smaller municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that your impression -- or the reasons for this was that there were quite a few Albanian soldiers and that it would not be safe. Along this route did you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, in the bushes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: About -- if you -- about how many soldiers did you see -- could you see?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Along the road before we were stopped, just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we'll get to the stop at the moment. How do you know this person you say was a soldier along the road before the stop was a soldier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, he wore a uniform, a cap, and he was unshaven and he carried a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's pretty clear. Can you just describe the uniform if you remember it, what type it was.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did any people on the bus react or comment when they saw that soldier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know -- well, I'll move on. Was -- you talked about a stop. You said this was before the stop. Tell me about the stop. Who stopped the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Six soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you describe - just in your own words, take your time - what you remember of how this stop occurred, where the soldiers were, what they did, what you saw.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: After I saw this one soldier, ten minutes later, it was near a mountain, six soldiers ran out on to the road before -- in front of the bus and stopped it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And very briefly can you describe how these soldiers were dressed and whether they were armed.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Two or three of them wore camouflage uniforms. The rest looked more like civilians. Two of them had bazookas and the rest carried automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did the driver do when these soldiers ran out of the bushes or ran out and stopped the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before he opened the door he said that we should not be afraid, that these were Albanian soldiers who were not killers like the Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did the people on the bus react at this point?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, some people were slightly upset. There was a bit of nervousness among the people on the bus. Mixed emotions on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, what happened after the driver opened the door to the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Three men boarded the bus. One of them said that we should get out our ID, our documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did they ask that to you personally or are you talking about collectively to the whole bus? Just describe a little bit what happened, what you remember.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They got on the bus and they said out loud that we should all take out our documents and hold them ready in our hands and that one of them would go through and check them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you take out an identification and hold it up?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What happened when your identification and your father's identification were checked by this soldier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He first started checking the identification of my mother and father because they were sitting in the front row, and he told my father to get off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he say why he was telling your father to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you about -- after he looked at your ID?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. He just looked at my ID and told me to get off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about your mother?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: She was crying and screaming, shouting to let us -- that they should let us go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did they, being the soldiers, do to your mother when she was crying and screaming like that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They pushed her away and trained a rifle on her, told her to shut up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you and your father get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did anybody else get off the bus or I should say ordered off the bus? Was anybody else told to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, two more people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We'll talk about them a little bit very soon, but do you know what ethnicity those two people were?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I had known one of them from around the town. I could tell from the way he was speaking that he was a Serb, and as for the other one I don't know, because we didn't talk to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: At this time when you were taken off the bus, what kind of clothing were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: A shirt, a pair of jeans, and sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: A shirt, jeans, and I think shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was anything that you and your father were wearing similar to a uniform? Could it be taken for a uniform?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. It was just regular clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You stated earlier when I first started talking with you that you'd never been in -- you'd never done any military service. Were you armed that day with any kind of weapon when you were taken off the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was your father or you a member of any kind of army, armed group, paramilitary or police force, any kind of armed organisation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The two other people who were ordered off the bus -- let's start with the first one who you said was a Serb who you'd seen around town. Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember his first name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, no. I really don't know his first name. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just so it's clear, what was your relationship with him before your -- before this event? I mean, can you describe whether you were friends, whether he was somebody you associated with or just how you knew who this person was.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, Djakovica is a small town and the number of non-Albanian population is pretty low. We all knew each other because there was only 2 per cent -- 2 per cent of the population was not Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And after you were ordered off the bus, the four of you, what happened with the bus?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: The driver got off -- in fact, he returned to the bus because he had gotten off when we did, and they told him to continue, to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, at this point had anybody told you why this was happening to you and your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. We didn't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were the soldiers doing with you after the bus left?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They lined us up against a wall and trained their rifles on us, on our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you speak to your father at all at this time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, I was frightened. I thought they would kill us, so I just told him I loved him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, the soldiers who you saw there, do you remember if they had any kind of insignia or badges or patches or anything like that on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, on their berets and some of them on their shoulders or on their chests they wore the insignia of their army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was that army called, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, what happened next? Did you or your father speak with any of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, since after they had taken away two other -- the two other men in an unknown direction, one of the soldiers asked us who we were and what we were doing there, and my father said that we used to live in Djakovica and that now we were moving out of Djakovica because that was not a good place to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What language did this conversation take place in?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: At first in Serbian. And after he asked my father where we were from and when my father said that he was from -- born in Slovenia and I was born in Zagreb, then the conversation continued in Slovenian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me go back a little bit. You said that the two other men were taken away in an unknown direction. Can you tell me, just for the record, which two men are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Genov and another Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How were they taken away? What kind of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was a Golf, a Volkswagen Golf. It was dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember, if you remember, what the registration plates were on that Golf, what country it was registered?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't recall the number, but it had Swiss licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We're just going to go through this step by step. What happened next? How long were you sitting there with your father -- your father talking to this soldier? What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, we were sitting there between half an hour and an hour, I'm not sure. We sat there with our heads bent until the Golf car returned to pick us up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then what happened? What happened after the Golf came back to pick you up?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They put us in the car, in the back, but some black bandannas over our head and eyes and drove us over a road that led through a forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long was this journey? How long before you get out of the car?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I really don't know. Perhaps an hour. I was very scared and I couldn't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's fine. Do you know which town you were in when this stop happened? Do you remember or did you know at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. I really didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Please tell me what happened after the car stopped and you were taken out of the car. Where were you taken? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: The car was parked in a village in front of a building that looked like a school. We were taken into one of the classrooms. And on the wall, to the side, I saw this third man who was with us. He was banging his head against the wall. His head was all covered in blood, and I think they had ordered him to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you remember when you met with the ICTY investigator and you gave your statement in 2003 he showed you some photos and you picked out some people you remembered?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you mean those who were in prison, detained, or members of the military?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm speaking now about whether you were shown pictures of people who were detained and that you remembered. Do you remember being shown those photos?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you remember that since I've met you that I showed you those same photos again. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now show the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, this should on your screen. I hope it does. And let me also -- let me know if you have any problems with that -- seeing that clearly and I can give you a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For the record, this is from P54, U003-2165.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man in that picture?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to show you another photo. P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Isn't that under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This one is not, Your Honour, this is one of the open ones. I'm sorry, I should have made that clear. I will show some photos from this exhibit which are under seal, however the photos I'm showing are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The next one I'd like to show you, Witness, to see if you recognise this person, again P54, U003-2164. Do you recognise that man, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was told his name later -- in fact, I know just his last name which is Cuk. I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Did you see Cuk in the school, the one which you're telling us about which you've just arrived at?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now -- again, you started to tell us, but what was he doing when you saw him in the school?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He was sitting on the floor banging his head against the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long did this go on for?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: For a long time. I think it may have been an hour, almost an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were there any guards in or around this schoolroom? Could you tell me where they were.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I really don't know how many of them were [as interpreted]. There were one or two soldiers inside the school, and outside of the school there were more of them, maybe about ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you and your father do when you came into this school?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: We sat in the last row of desks and we just kept quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who else was sitting in that schoolroom, in that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was he doing at this point?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He also sat there in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now -- again, at this point when you're brought into the school, have any of those soldiers or guards told you why you're being taken to this school or how long you're going to be there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. They didn't tell us anything. They just told us to sit there and be quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I should have asked you this earlier. About what time of day is it now that you're at this school?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what the time was, but it was early in the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did you spend in the school? How long were you held there, you and your father and the other man?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, around four or five hours. It was late at night when they took us away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you asked -- were you and your father asked any questions while you were there in the school by the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: The basic questions. Who we were, what we were doing in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you speak to these soldiers as well or did your father speak, both of you? Can you explain, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, it was mainly my father who was talking to them because the soldier who guarded them -- who guarded us told them that my father was a Slovene and that we were Croats. And then they asked us what we were doing in Kosovo and where we were going on that bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did your father say about where you were going and what you were going to do?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He said that we were moving out of Kosovo, that we were going back to Belgrade in order to move out to a third country.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what happened to Genov? What did you see happen to him in that schoolroom?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, the mistreatment started perhaps after an hour. Whoever went by him hit him, and sometimes they would take him out of the classroom and beat him in the hall of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see him being -- Genov being beaten in the hall or hear it? Can you describe how you knew he was being beaten out in the hallway?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, we heard the blows and we heard him screaming from the pain, begging them to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long did this last?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, they beat him from the moment when they brought us to the school until they took us away further, although with interruptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did Genov speak to your father at all while he was in the school?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He asked him at one point whether my father would hide his military ID because he was afraid that they would find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did your father say?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He said that he didn't dare do it, that he was with his son, but that if he wanted to he could go out in front of the house in the toilet and throw it into the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you say that he wanted to -- he could go out in the front of the house and throw the ID away, he meaning Genov could do it or he meaning your father could do it? Just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: He meant Genov because they did let us go out to the toilet, so my father recommended that to Genov, that he, Genov, go out himself to the toilet and throw the ID into the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether these soldiers actually found Genov's ID or whether they didn't?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They did. After several hours of beating, I believe that due to the beating the ID fell out of his pocket or they found it in his pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They stopped beating him. They said something in Albanian and then a soldier came to my father, an older soldier went to my father and asked him, Is this a police ID?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did your father say?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, since he didn't have his glasses and the picture was black and white, my father said, It looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then what happened? What happened to Genov after that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: They went on beating him with automatic rifles, sharp objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how did that end? At some point how did they -- when did they stop beating him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: When he passed out and when it looked as if their beating had killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did you feel when you saw this beating of Genov?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, I was frightened. I was 18 years old. I didn't know what would happen to me and my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to ask you to tell us what happened Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. next and tell me how you came to leave the school and where you went. Let me just say, if you want to take a short break, I'm sure you could ask and the Court would understand. So just let me know at any --

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. No, there is no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Then tell me, please, how you and your father ended up leaving this schoolroom.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was already nighttime and a combi van parked there and they said that they would drive us somewhere else, to a different locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You've -- I'm sorry, I should have asked you one other question. You've told us what you saw and what you heard in the schoolroom. Were you and your -- or your father physically mistreated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm sorry I interrupted you. The combi van came up. Did you get into the van?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, first they told us to get up and then they took us to the trucks and they put sacks over our heads and tied them at our waists.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you say "us," are you talking about the four people who were taken off the bus, the same group?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. The three of us. They carried Genov into the van.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you told where you were being taken?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you told how long it was going to be before you could be free again, see your mother again?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long, as far as you can remember, did this trip last when you were put in the combi van?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Perhaps between 45 minutes and an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you remember, could you tell whether -- what kind of roads you were driving over, whether they were paved or dirt, or whether you were on a road at all?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. I know that it was a bumpy road like a village road through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And to the final destination, and we'll get to that later, where you are allowed to get out of the van, were there any stops along the way?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: There were stops every few minutes because of some kind of checks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What happened at those stops as far as you could tell? I realise you had a sack over your head, but what was your impression of what was happening at those stops?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite sure what they were saying, but it sounded like some kind of greeting and some kind of check, some kind of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've neglected to ask you one question. I'm sorry, I have to ask you again about what happened to Genov in the school. While he was being beaten by these soldiers, do you remember whether they said anything to him or asked him any questions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at the end of this ride in the car, what happens? Can you tell me when eventually the hood is taken off and you're able to see again.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, after the drive they stopped the vehicle and they took the sack off my head and I saw a big brown fence and gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And at that point did you have any idea where you were? What village, or what place you were in?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now show the witness I think it's from P6, U008-3680. It's labelled A8.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just take a moment and look at that picture. I'll give you a hard copy because on my screen it's not very clear. Can you tell me what you see in that picture, what's depicted there.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: The inside of the gate and a village house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I showed you that photo here when you met me a couple days ago. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What happened after the combi pulled in -- well -- pulled in through this gate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, it parked in front of the door. Then the truck door opened and they got us off the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who got off? Who was -- who got off?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: All who were inside; their soldiers, my father, I. They carried Genov and there was the fourth man.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the fourth man is the one you identified as Cuk. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then where did you go? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, they did us in to this house, the ground floor, and they kept us in a room down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honours. Sorry. Your Honour, may we go into private session for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of December, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
